consumerRule: Only a 404 whose code is ASSET_NOT_FOUND from Assets maps to UNRESOLVED. Any other failure of the lookup (a 404 PATH_NOT_FOUND, a 500, a timeout, the service being down, or a 400 for a malformed id) is a lookup failure: the consumer shows an error entry with a null asset and never shows UNRESOLVED, so an outage or a wrong path cannot pass for a dataset of missing assets. A Missions reference with no entry in the mapping is a mapping failure: Assets is not asked, and the consumer never shows it as UNRESOLVED.

idAssignment.rule: The assets of release 1.0, taken in the order of their release 1.0 identifiers (the letter prefix as text, then the number as a number), receive the native identifiers AST-0001, AST-0002 and so on, one step each. A parent keeps pointing at the same asset under its new identifier. The same rule gives the same identifiers every time, and the manifest pins the assets of release 1.0 it was applied to.

idConvention.AST: every asset of the Assets system (the native prefix); the grammar allows other prefixes of capital letters joined by single underscores for the future
idConvention.Missions-local references: SH-17, EQ-64, VS-31 and the like belong to Missions, as C-85 does for crew: Assets neither stores nor accepts them, and the mapping to an Assets id belongs to the integration layer

limitations: Synthetic lab content: no claim of canon.
The expected mapping is a statement of what the integration layer should do, written here so that its result can be checked; Assets stores no Missions reference and offers no mapping.
Kinds, statuses and parents of the Missions-referenced assets are decided by this dataset; Missions holds its own references only.
No timing judgment: DESTROYED and MISSING assets resolve with their status.
No location, no Personnel mapping and no cross-service rule beyond the references shown.
